title: How to Avoid the Top 5 Phone Scams Targeting Seniors in 2026
bigPicture: Scammers call pretending to be someone you trust. If you pause and verify, you can protect yourself every time.
whatYouNeedToKnow: The Grandparent Scam: Someone calls saying 'Grandma, it's me' and asks for money fast. They hope you'll act before thinking.
The Fake Government Call: A caller says they're from the IRS or Medicare and threatens fines or jail. Real agencies never call to threaten you.
The Tech Support Scam: A pop-up or call says your computer is infected. They ask for remote access or payment to 'fix' it.
The Prize or Lottery Scam: You 'won' a vacation or cash but must pay a fee first. Real prizes never ask you to pay to claim them.
The Family Emergency Scam: A caller says your child or relative is hurt or in jail and needs bail money right now.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Sending money or gift cards before checking the story with a family member.
Giving out personal info like your Social Security number over an unexpected call.
Pressing buttons or calling back numbers from suspicious voicemails.
Believing a caller because they know your name — scammers find names online easily.
actionSteps: Hang up. It is okay to end a call that feels pushy or scary.
Call back the person directly using a number you already know, not one they gave you.
Ask a trusted family member or friend before sending any money.
Register your number on the National Do Not Call Registry at donotcall.gov.
Save a trusted contact's number in your phone under 'ICE' (In Case of Emergency) for quick verification.
